# QS-CFW-8165-49 - Quality specification - flange blank CFW-8165-49 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-8165-49

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection method, and nonconformance handling for flange blank CFW-8165-49 manufactured from alloy 4140 at Plant P2. It applies to all production lots and to material released for machining operations. The intent is to ensure the flange blank meets metallurgical and dimensional conditions necessary for downstream processing and final part performance.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria / Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4140 | Verify mill test report matches order. |
| Hardness | 36-42 HRC. | Hardness to be measured on machined or flat ground surface representative of forged condition. Accept if hardness falls within range. If readings border tolerance limits, verify with an additional measurement at an adjacent location. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.06 mm. | Verify bore diameter with calibrated bore gage or plug gage compatible with specified nominal bore. Accept if measured diameter falls within tolerance band. |
| Maximum forging weight | 25.2 kg. | Reject any individual forging that exceeds maximum forging weight at time of part release. Weigh on calibrated scale; record mass on inspection report. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cracks, and cold shuts that would affect machining or final integrity. | Localized surface imperfections that can be removed by normal machining and do not materially change the geometry are acceptable after documented disposition. |

Inspection method
- Sampling and frequency: Inspect representative parts from each production lot prior to release for machining. Use risk-based sampling consistent with quality system practice. When process changes occur, include full dimensional and hardness verification on first shipment after change.
- Hardness measurement: Prepare a flat area free of scale and heavy flash. Use a Rockwell hardness tester capable of reading Rockwell C scale. Apply test load according to equipment procedure and record values in the inspection record. Take a minimum of two readings on each part in locations representative of bulk material, avoiding edges and features. If the two readings differ materially, take a third reading and record all values with location notes. Final acceptance requires the recorded readings to be within 36-42 HRC.
- Bore measurement: Clean bore to remove scale and any burrs. Measure using a calibrated bore gage or calibrated go/no-go plug gage appropriate for the nominal bore dimension. Report measured diameter and note measurement instrument and calibration identifier. Acceptance is based on the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm.
- Weight verification: Use a calibrated industrial scale. Place part on scale in a stable orientation that does not add fixtures or supports that contribute measurable mass. Record the mass and ensure value does not exceed 25.2 kg. If a part exceeds 25.2 kg, segregate and tag for disposition.
- Visual inspection: Use adequate lighting and magnification as needed. Document any surface anomalies with photographs and descriptive notes. For discontinuities that are not clearly acceptable, perform supplementary evaluation per nonconformance handling below.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification: Segregate nonconforming parts immediately and tag with a unique nonconformance identifier. Record the nature of the nonconformance, measurement data, inspection instruments used, inspector name, and date.
- Examples and disposition rationale:
  - Example: A flange blank measures 35 HRC on two hardness readings and 36 HRC on a third. Because 35 HRC is outside the requirement of 36-42 HRC., the part is nonconforming. Disposition options include reheat/heat treatment to achieve the required hardness band, scrap if further processing is impractical, or use as scrap material. Any heat treatment disposition must be approved by engineering and documented.
  - Example: A bore measurement shows a deviation greater than ±0.06 mm. The part is nonconforming for dimensional tolerance. Disposition may include rework if machining allowance exists and the feature can be brought into tolerance without violating other requirements. If rework is not viable, the part shall be rejected.
  - Example: A forge weighing 25.4 kg is over the maximum forging weight of 25.2 kg. The part is rejected and segregated. Investigate process variables that allowed excess mass and take corrective action.
- Disposition process: Fill out the nonconformance report and notify quality engineering. For potential rework or repair, provide an engineering evaluation that documents the corrective action method, verification steps, and final acceptance criteria. Only quality engineering may authorize return to production.
- Records and traceability: Maintain the following records for each lot and for any nonconforming disposition:
  - Mill test report or material certificate for the lot.
  - Hardness readings with instrument identification and calibration status.
  - Bore diameter measurements, instrument identification, and calibration status.
  - Weight measurement with scale identifier and calibration status.
  - Visual inspection notes and photographs where applicable.
  - Nonconformance reports and final disposition documentation including engineering approvals.
- Corrective actions: For repeated nonconformances, perform root cause analysis, implement corrective actions, and track effectiveness. Document corrective actions, responsible parties, and verification results in the lot history.

Records to keep
- Inspection records for each lot shall be retained in the document control system and include all items listed under Records and traceability. Records shall be sufficient to allow trace-back to raw material batch and individual part where practical. Maintain photographic records for visual defects that require engineering disposition.

Background and rationale
- The hardness requirement of 36-42 HRC. is selected to ensure the forged microstructure and mechanical properties are suitable for subsequent machining, heat treatment, and service loading for parts machined from flange blank CFW-8165-49. The bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm. ensures the feature can be machined to final drawing dimensions without excessive stock removal or rework. The maximum forging weight of 25.2 kg. is set to confirm forging press capacity, handling limits, and tooling compatibility in Plant P2 operations.

Revision control
- This is Revision Rev C of QS-CFW-8165-49. Implement changes as directed by quality management and record revision history in the document control log.
